config.title: Dentist in Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: What public insurance pays at a Berlin dentist, how the Bonusheft changes your share, and where to go on a weekend.

items.q: What does public health insurance pay at the dentist in Berlin?
items.a: Two check-ups a year, tartar removal once a year, standard fillings and gum disease screening every two years, all billed directly to your Krankenkasse. Professional cleaning is usually private, though many Kassen pay a yearly allowance towards it.

Your dentist stamps it at each check-up. With a check-up in each of the five calendar years before a treatment starts, the fixed subsidy for crowns, bridges and dentures rises from 60% to 70%. With ten unbroken years it rises to 75%.

items.q: Does a missing check-up in 2020 break my Bonusheft?
items.a: No. The law exempts 2020 because of the pandemic, so a missing stamp for that year does not break the five-year or the ten-year chain.

items.q: What if I missed one year?
items.a: For the 70% level you need all five of the last calendar years. For 75%, your Krankenkasse may still grant it with exactly one missed year in ten if your teeth show regular care, but it is a discretionary decision and you have to ask.

items.q: How much does the Krankenkasse pay for a crown in 2026?
items.a: For a crown on a badly damaged back tooth, €239.03 at the base rate, €278.87 with the five-year bonus and €298.79 with the ten-year bonus. The amount is fixed, so a more expensive crown leaves you with a bigger share.

items.q: I lost my Bonusheft. What now?
items.a: Ask your practice to fill in a new booklet from its patient records. If you have changed dentists, ask each old practice for the years they saw you.

items.q: Where do I find an emergency dentist in Berlin at the weekend?
items.a: Call the on-call hotline on 030 89004-333. On weekends and public holidays every district has one dentist on duty from 9:00 to 12:00 and another from 15:00 to 18:00, and the Charité dental clinic on Aßmannshauser Straße covers extra evening hours.
